definitions.explanation: A document created by a private individual or organization, as opposed to an official or public document issued by a government body. In legal contexts, this distinction is important because forging private documents and public documents carry different penalties.

examples.japanese: {契約書|けいやくしょ}は{私文書|しぶんしょ}に{分類|ぶんるい}される。
examples.english: Contracts are classified as private documents.

examples.japanese: {私文書|しぶんしょ}{偽造|ぎぞう}は{犯罪|はんざい}だ。
examples.english: Forging a private document is a crime.

examples.japanese: {私文書|しぶんしょ}であっても、{署名|しょめい}や{押印|おういん}があれば{法的|ほうてき}な{効力|こうりょく}を{持|も}つことがある。
examples.english: Even a private document can have legal validity if it bears a signature or seal.

notes:
Compound of {私|し} (private; personal) and {文書|ぶんしょ} (document). The reading {文書|ぶんしょ} becomes しぶんしょ as a compound. In Japanese law, the distinction between {私文書|しぶんしょ} and {公文書|こうぶんしょ} (public/official document) is significant — {公文書偽造|こうぶんしょぎぞう} carries a heavier penalty than {私文書偽造|しぶんしょぎぞう}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {私文書偽造|しぶんしょぎぞう}: forgery of a private document
- {私文書|しぶんしょ}の{作成|さくせい}: creation of a private document
- {私文書|しぶんしょ}と{公文書|こうぶんしょ}: private and public documents

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {公文書|こうぶんしょ}: public/official document, issued by a government body
- {書類|しょるい}: documents in general, without the legal private/public distinction
- {証書|しょうしょ}: certificate or deed, a formal document attesting to something
